Infra & Chips.content: # From Scale-Up and Scale-Out to Scale-In: How Agentic AI Is Redefining NVIDIA’s AI Factory Network Architecture ∙ Paid Over the past several years, one of the central questions in AI infrastructure has been simple: **How do we connect more GPUs together?** From NVIDIA NVLink and NVSwitch for Scale-Up networking to InfiniBand and Spectrum-X Ethernet for Scale-Out, much of the investment in AI data-center networking has focused on the same fundamental challenge. As model sizes increase and GPU clusters expand from hundreds to tens or even hundreds of thousands of accelerators, the network must ensure that these expensive compute resources remain highly utilized rather than spending valuable time waiting for data. With the arrival of Agentic AI, however, the nature of the problem is beginning to change. The next generation of AI factories will need to scale far more than GPUs. As AI evolves from Generative AI toward Agentic AI and eventually Multi-Agent AI, the traffic profile inside the data center becomes fundamentally different. An AI agent completing a task may repeatedly perform model inference, query databases, access storage, call APIs, read and write memory, validate security policies, and communicate with other agents. As a result, the bottleneck of an AI factory is gradually moving outward from the GPU itself. This is the context behind NVIDIA’s introduction of a new architectural concept: **Scale-In networking.** If Scale-Up addresses the question of how many GPUs can behave like one larger logical GPU, Scale-Out addresses how many GPU servers can operate together as a large cluster, and Scale-Across addresses how multiple data centers can function as a larger distributed AI factory, then Scale-In addresses a different problem: **How can users, applications, agents, data, storage, security, and the control plane scale together with accelerated computing?** Scale-In should therefore not be understood as simply another GPU interconnect. Instead, it represents a fundamental redefinition of the traditional front-end network. Infra & Chips.content: # CoreWeave: Vera Rubin NVL72 Has Arrived ### Cognition is First Production Customer, CoreWeave Offers NVIDIA Vera CPU for Agentic AI [Rich Miller](https://substack.com/@richmiller) NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 racks running in a CoreWeave data center. (Photo: CoreWeave) **CoreWeave** says it has brought its first customer online using the NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 rack, the latest and most advanced AI computing systems offered by NVIDIA. AI specialist **Cognition** is now using the new Vera Rubin NVL72 systems in production, CoreWeave [announced](https://www.coreweave.com/news/coreweave-delivers-nvidia-vera-rubin-nvl72-performance-at-production-scale-starting-with-cognition) at its Fully Connected conference Wednesday, saying Cognition was the “first customer anywhere” running production workloads on the new system. > “Bringing up NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 so quickly, and having a customer already seeing performance gains within days, is the payoff from years of engineering our platform across GPU generations,” said Chen Goldberg, executive vice president of product & engineering at CoreWeave. CoreWeave also said it will offer [the NVIDIA Vera CPU](https://www.coreweave.com/news/coreweave-to-offer-nvidia-vera-the-first-cpu-built-for-ai-agents), which is optimized for CPU-intensive agentic AI workloads. ## Pushing Boundaries NVIDIA says the [Vera Rubin platform](https://datacenterrichness.substack.com/p/vera-rubin-enters-production-what) is the most tightly integrated AI data center design yet, using “extreme co-design” to squeeze every bit of performance and energy efficiency out of racks, servers and chips. Cognition says it is already seeing significant performance gains for Devin, its AI agent for software engineering. > “By deploying the NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 on CoreWeave, our engineers are seeing up to a 4.8 times increase in total token throughput for SWE-2 inference workloads” compared to a GB200 NVL72 baseline, said Silas Alberti, SVP research & founding team at Cognition. With its base of AI customers focused on high-density computing, CoreWeave has been an early adopter of the latest NVIDIA technology. Other cloud AI platforms are also planning to bring the Vera Rubin platform online during 2026, including AWS, Google Cloud, Microsoft Oracle, Lambda, Nebius and Nscale. > “CoreWeave has consistently demonstrated the infrastructure expertise required to bring each new generation of NVIDIA accelerated computing into production,” said Ian Buck, vice president of Hyperscale and High-Performance Computing at **NVIDIA**.
